features.name: Job Aggregation Engine
features.description: Aggregates listings from LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, and niche tech boards via their public APIs and RSS feeds; updates every 15 minutes; de‑duplicates based on title, company, and posting ID. Acceptance: >95% of active listings appear within 30 minutes of posting. Success metric: 10,000 unique listings per day with <2% duplicate rate. Non‑functional: API rate‑limit handling, GDPR‑compliant data storage.

features.name: AI Resume Tailoring
features.description: Parses a user's master resume (PDF/Word) using NLP, extracts skills, experiences, and achievements; re‑writes bullet points to match each job description using a fine‑tuned LLM. Acceptance: Tailored resume scores ≥80% similarity to recruiter‑preferred keywords (measured by ElasticSearch relevance). Success metric: 70% of users report higher interview callbacks after first use. Integration: OpenAI API (or self‑hosted LLM), resume parsing library (e.g., ResumeParser).

features.name: One‑Click Application Launcher
features.description: Generates a pre‑filled application payload (cover letter, tailored resume, required fields) and submits it via the job board’s application API or simulated browser automation where API is unavailable. Acceptance: Application submission succeeds ≥98% of attempts; user receives real‑time confirmation. Success metric: Average time from job match to submission <30 seconds.

features.name: Applicant Dashboard & Tracker
features.description: Provides a Kanban‑style view (Applied, In Review, Interview, Rejected) with auto‑updates from board APIs and email parsing; includes analytics on response rates and timeline heatmaps. Acceptance: Dashboard reflects status changes within 5 minutes of external update. Success metric: 80% of users log in ≥3 times/week.

features.name: Recruiter Candidate Feed
features.description: Exports a filtered list of platform candidates to recruiter ATS (Greenhouse, Lever) via webhook; includes AI‑generated fit score and key skill tags. Acceptance: Feed integrates without data loss; fit score correlates ≥0.7 with recruiter manual rating. Success metric: 30% increase in qualified candidate pool for early‑adopter recruiters.

payload.feedback:
The deliverable is a solid start – it includes a clear value proposition, three well‑defined personas, a prioritized feature list with descriptions, acceptance criteria, and user stories. However, it falls short of being fully specific, complete, and actionable for product development. Missing or weak areas include:
1. **Non‑functional requirements** beyond GDPR (e.g., performance, scalability, reliability, security, accessibility, and data retention policies).
2. **Technical architecture & stack** – no diagram or description of how components (aggregation engine, AI services, automation layer, dashboards, recruiter feed) will be hosted, communicate, or be scaled.
3. **MVP scope & roadmap** – no indication of which features belong in the Minimum Viable Product, release milestones, or timeline.
4. **Integration details** – API authentication methods, rate‑limit strategies, fallback mechanisms for sites without public APIs, and specifics on ATS webhook contracts are absent.
5. **Metrics & KPIs** – success metrics are listed per feature but there is no overarching product‑level KPI hierarchy, target numbers, or measurement plan.
6. **Risk & mitigation** – no identification of technical or market risks (e.g., job‑board API changes, LLM hallucination, legal compliance) or mitigation strategies.
7. **User onboarding & flow** – missing step‑by‑step user journey (signup, resume upload, preference setup, daily match delivery, application submission confirmation).
8. **Pricing & business model** – no discussion of how the platform will monetize (subscription tiers, per‑application fees, recruiter licensing, etc.).
9. **Competitive analysis** – no reference to existing solutions or differentiation points beyond the generic value proposition.
10. **Regulatory & legal considerations** – beyond GDPR, no mention of data consent flows, opt‑out mechanisms, or employment law compliance across jurisdictions.
To make the output truly actionable, these gaps need to be addressed with concrete specifications, diagrams, timelines, and validation plans.
